why.text: Climate, ground and local grapes favour full ripening. Reds are fruity and structured, whites fresh.

styles.text: Fruity, structured reds, aromatic rosados, fresh whites, and white and rosé sparkling wines.

climate.text: Conditions favour full ripening and high sugar concentration.

tastes.text: Reds: fruity, possible vegetal, floral or mineral notes; structure, balance, some persistence. Rosés: fruity; balance, some persistence. Whites: fruity, Moscatel varietal; balance, good intensity.

styles.name: Crianza
styles.text: Barrel ageing adds wood and spice aromas.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Fruity aromas; fresh, fine, lively whites; aromatic, persistent rosés.

why.text: Sea-level island vineyards get freshness, humidity and salt from the Embat wind. High sun and limy soils give aromatic, high-alcohol wines with integrated acidity.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, liqueur wines, and sparkling and semi-sparkling wines.

climate.text: Island, almost at sea level; the Embat wind brings freshness, humidity and salt; strong sunshine. No figures given.

soil.text: Limy (calcareous) soils, which boost aromatic compounds.

tastes.text: Whites and rosés: bright, fresh and fruity; barrel-aged whites voluminous and unctuous. Reds: medium-high colour; fresh fruit when young, ripe fruit with oak when aged; elegant, fleshy, velvety.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Straw-green to golden whites with floral, syrupy fruit; reds red to purple.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Tiny bubbles in long chains; aromas of ageing on the lees.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Fine bubbles; fruity with second-fermentation aromas; fresh.
